title: Andrews 'torn' as Brentford keep Premier League unbeaten run intact
subtitle: Keith Andrews was left "torn" after his Brentford side continued their unbeaten Premier League run with a 2-2 draw at Aston Villa.
paragraphs: Brentford boss Keith Andrews was left "torn" after seeing his side salvage a point against Aston Villa in a 2-2 draw at Villa Park.
In an enthralling Premier League encounter, Yehor Yarmoliuk gave the visitors the lead in the 10th minute before Nicolas Jackson netted an equaliser 88 seconds later.
John McGinn scored Villa's second 13 minutes from time, as his effort took a massive deflection off Kristoffer Ajer, who redeemed himself moments later, slotting home from close range.
The result sees Brentford sit fourth in the Premier League table, and continuing their unbeaten run in the competition.
The Bees are also undefeated in their last eight games in the Premier League, but have lost eight points from winning position in the process, with only Bournemouth (nine) having lost more.
However, it was mixed emotions for Andrews, whose side mustered an expected goals (xG) of 1.25 from 14 shots.

"[I am] Torn to be honest. I liked a lot today - spirit, grit, determination. There was evidence of rustiness, which is understandable, but I don't like to use that as an excuse, but the boys have been away for three weeks so it's trying to find the balance," said Andrews.
"Then we had Kevin's [Shade] injury, Jannik [Schuster] wasn't right and came off at half time, so we got tested today.
“But we're also up against a team who I thought were just starting to click before the international break.
“But the fact that we're disappointed coming away from home to a Champions League team who spend big money tells you a lot."

Meanwhile, Unai Emery considered the result to be fair, even though Aston Villa have now failed to win any of their opening three home games in a league campaign for the first time since 2015-16, when they were without a win in their first nine league matches at Villa Park (D3 L6).

Reflecting on the game, Emery said, “To draw at home is not a good result. I think we played a match with a lot of things improved from our last home match against [Nottingham] Forest. We created chances but conceded more chances than I expected.
“Maybe the result is fair, but analysing how we are improving things, competing better, I can't tell nothing to the players about the match.
“We'll try to analyse again how we can improve even more. A better match than against Forest. Keep going forward.
"We tried, we pushed, we had chances but so did they. At the end we could've won, but also we could've lost."
Emery will be hoping for different fortunes come Tuesday, as his side host Fenerbahce in the Champions League on Wednesday.
